title: fix(service-settings): Setup → Authentication says what the sign-up and Google toggles do
body:
Fixes #24776

Clause-②: no

## What changes

Setup → Authentication showed two controls that read as contradicting the system on a fresh install. Both are still truthful about what the runtime does; what they lacked is the second condition. This PR states it. **Only wording changes.** No default, `visible` rule, `required` flag, option or stored key moves. The admission matrix below is byte-identical before and after.

- **`auth.signup_enabled`**: relabelled *Allow email sign-up* (was *Allow self-service registration*), and it now has help text. The help says the toggle opens the email-and-password sign-up form, and the *Self-registration audience* decides who that form admits:
  - `invite_only`: only an address holding a pending invitation;
  - `email_domain`: the allowlisted domains, plus invited addresses;
  - `open`: anyone.

  Off closes the form under every audience, invitations included.
- **`auth.google_enabled`**: the help says Google sign-in is offered only once a client ID and a client secret both resolve, either saved on the page or from `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` on the server (the server values win over saved ones). Until both resolve, the login page shows no Google button, even while the toggle is on. Off withdraws Google even when the server sets both.
- The `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES` bundles carry the new label and help. `en` matters too: the console resolves `settings.auth.keys.KEY.label` / `.help` from the served bundle *before* the manifest literal, so if `en` lagged, the English page would keep showing the old text.

Files: `packages/services/service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts`, `auth.manifest.test.ts`, `src/translations/{en,zh-CN,ja-JP,es-ES}.ts`, `.changeset/24776-auth-settings-signup-google-help.md` (patch, `@objectstack/service-settings`). Nothing under `plugin-auth/src`, `settings-service.ts`, `settings-service-plugin.ts`, `packages/spec` or objectui is written.

## What was measured (the card's premise holds)

**The composition:** the real `SettingsService` with the real auth manifest, the real `AuthPlugin` booted init → start → `kernel:ready`, and the real better-auth pipeline over an in-memory engine. `bindAuthSettings` reads that service. Each cell boots fresh with one existing human (so the bootstrap bypass is off), a pending invitation for `invitee@elsewhere.org`, and `member_default` as the declared self-registration set. The probes:
- `POST /api/v1/auth/sign-up/email` through `manager.handleRequest`;
- `getPublicConfig()` (what `/auth/config` serves the login page);
- `SettingsService.get` (what the page shows).

The instrument was a one-off test file and is not committed.

**H2 — `signup_enabled` × `audience_posture`.** "unset" is the manifest default, read with source `default`. Every cell has zero bind refusals.

| signup_enabled | audience_posture | stranger@acme.com | stranger@elsewhere.org | invitee (pending invitation) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unset / true | unset / invite_only | 403 SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED | 403 SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED | admitted |
| unset / true | email_domain (acme.com) | admitted | 403 EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED | admitted |
| unset / true | open | admitted | admitted | admitted |
| false | unset / invite_only | 403 SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED | 403 SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED | 400 EMAIL_PASSWORD_SIGN_UP_DISABLED |
| false | email_domain | 400 EMAIL_PASSWORD_SIGN_UP_DISABLED | 403 EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED | 400 EMAIL_PASSWORD_SIGN_UP_DISABLED |
| false | open | 400 EMAIL_PASSWORD_SIGN_UP_DISABLED | 400 EMAIL_PASSWORD_SIGN_UP_DISABLED | 400 EMAIL_PASSWORD_SIGN_UP_DISABLED |
| env `OS_AUTH_SIGNUP_ENABLED=false` | open | 400 | 400 | 400 |
| env `OS_DISABLE_SIGNUP=true` | open | 400 | 400 | 400 |
| unset | env `OS_AUTH_AUDIENCE_POSTURE=open` | admitted | admitted | admitted |

(The table folds pairs of cells that read the same. The record has 15 separate rows: 12 stored-or-default, plus 3 env.)

So `signup_enabled` is a door of its own, in series with the posture. `false` closes what the posture alone leaves open, and under `invite_only` it still decides whether an invited address can register through the form. Unset reads as `true` and an unset posture reads as `invite_only`, so the page's defaults already show the runtime's effective state. The contradiction was only in the wording.

**H3 — Google.** No `GOOGLE_*` value is printed anywhere; the instrument set fake values in-process.

| shape | save | page shows | login offers Google | client id wired from |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no credentials anywhere, google keys unset (the tester's shape) | — | ON, both fields empty | no | — |
| env credentials, `google_enabled` unset | — | ON, both fields empty | **yes** | env |
| env credentials + save `google_enabled: true` | **refused** `google_client_id/required`, `google_client_secret/required` | ON, empty | yes | env |
| env credentials + stored `google_enabled: false` | ok | OFF | no | — |
| env credentials + `OS_AUTH_GOOGLE_ENABLED=false` | — | OFF (env) | no | — |
| no credentials + save `google_enabled: true` | refused (required) | ON, empty | no | — |
| stored credentials, `google_enabled` unset | ok | ON, both SET | yes | stored |
| stored credentials + stored `google_enabled: false` | ok | OFF | no | — |
| env AND stored credentials, `google_enabled` unset | ok | ON, both SET | yes | env |

The env-credential deployment with an unset toggle signs in with Google, both before and after this PR. No default moves.

**Before / after.** Base `87c09ebb7a` vs head `fbf586d971`: the 26-line record is byte-identical (`diff` exit 0; sha256 `74e45ec11dd103de…` on both sides). A control line from the after-run reads the edited manifest (`signup_enabled.label=Allow email sign-up`), which proves that run loaded the change it claims to compare.

## Why this route (decision frame: business need · long-term · AI-proofing · startup scope)

**`signup_enabled`.** Chosen: relabel plus help text stating the conjunction.
- **Hide it under `invite_only` (`visible`)**: rejected. The matrix shows the toggle decides the invitee column there. A stored `false` hidden under `invite_only` would keep invited people out with the cause off-screen.
- **Default `false`**: rejected. The runtime's default is open (`disableSignUp` unset). The page would read OFF over an open form, and the first save that carried the shown value would close the invitee door, which is a narrowing this card may not make.
- **Retire the key**: not applicable. It has a reader and an effect of its own (the whole `false` row).
- **On the four axes:** the chosen route serves a measured need (the tester's reading); it adds no surface (one description, one label); and its pin ties the help to the posture option table, so a posture added later reds until the help covers it.

**`google_enabled`.** Chosen: help text stating the conjunction.
- **Default `false`**: rejected on measurement. It reads OFF on the two shapes that do offer Google (env credentials with the toggle unset; stored credentials with the toggle unset), and its `visible` rule would hide the stored credentials there. The runtime reads explicit values only, so its behaviour would not move; the page would simply stop telling the truth on those shapes.
- **A conditional `info_banner`**: rejected. It is one more specifier and eight more strings, and it cannot see env credentials either, so its text would hedge exactly as the help does.
- **Have the settings resolver report `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` as an env source for the two keys**: this would let the page show "Set via env", but it lives in `settings-service.ts` or the spec. Both are outside this claim. It is raised in the report as an open question, with the save refusal below.

## Pins and ablation

`auth.manifest.test.ts` gains three cases:
1. `signup_enabled` keeps default `true` and its `email_password_enabled`-only `visible` rule, and its help names every `audience_posture` option value (read from the option table) and the select's label.
2. `google_enabled` keeps default `true`, and its help names `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`.
3. The `en` bundle carries the manifest label and help verbatim for both keys.

Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, one leg per changed declaration, run on the committed head `fbf586d971`). Each leg was mutated, run red, then restored, with the restore proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`:
- delete `under invite_only, …; ` from the `signup_enabled` help → 2 failed / 13 passed (cases 1 and 3); restored to blob `1fc310c429e5`.
- replace `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET on the server` with `credentials on the server` → 2 failed / 13 passed (cases 2 and 3); restored to blob `1fc310c429e5`.
- revert the `en` label to `Allow self-service registration` → 1 failed / 14 passed (case 3); restored to blob `8784d7d80de3`.

The test imports the manifest and bundle by relative path, so it reads `src/`: no build or `dist/` leg is involved.

## Verification (head `fbf586d971`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` → 53 files, 897 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings run typecheck` → exit 0. `tsc --listFiles` counts `auth.manifest.test.ts` in the program once.
- Derived gates (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, 66 commands): 65 exit 0. `--ran` reports 66 accounted, 65 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN.
- NOT MEASURED: `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, reason: PREREQUISITE NOT MET (exit 3). It reads every package's `dist/`, and this worktree built only the service-settings / plugin-auth closure. CI runs it.
- Not run locally, declared to CI: `test:repo`; plugin-auth's suite, because this diff writes nothing there and changes only manifest strings.
- `main` moved four commits past the base while this ran; none of them touches service-settings or plugin-auth, so the branch is not re-merged.

## Acceptance notes

- **Save refusal on env-credential deployments (handed to the seat as a finding).** On a deployment whose Google credentials come from `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, saving `google_enabled: true` from the console is refused (`google_client_id/required`, `google_client_secret/required`) while the login page offers Google. So an admin who switches Google off on the page cannot switch it back on there without re-typing credentials the server already holds. This PR leaves `required` alone, because that is save-validation territory.
- **The old label overclaimed (code reading only, not measured end to end).** `signup_enabled` binds `emailAndPassword.disableSignUp`, which better-auth consults only on the email sign-up route (`dist/api/routes/sign-up.mjs`). Social sign-up reads the provider's own flag (`dist/api/routes/callback.mjs`), so *Allow self-service registration* overstated what the switch closes. The new label names what it actually controls.
- **Group descriptions not touched.** The `email_password` group description ("…and self-service registration") and the `membership` group description ("Pairs with self-service registration above") still use the old phrase. They are outside this claim's specifiers. Carrier: none.
